task_instance: Write a Packer HCL template (ami.pkr.hcl) for building an Ubuntu 22.04 AMI via the amazon-ebs builder, then run `packer init`, `packer validate`, and `packer build` on it to actually produce a custom AMI, as the skill describes.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable requires the HashiCorp Packer CLI (and its amazon-ebs plugin) to init/validate/build the template. `packer` is not installed anywhere on this machine (`which packer` -> not found; `find / -iname '*packer*'` only turns up unrelated JS npm packages named 'packer.js' inside pngjs/expo devtools, not the HashiCorp binary). Installing Packer or fetching the amazon plugin requires network/package-registry access, which this offline workstation does not have. Even if Packer were present, `packer build` would need to call the live AWS EC2 API to launch an instance, create an EBS volume/snapshot, and register an AMI, which needs real AWS credentials and network access to AWS - both unavailable/forbidden in this sandbox. So the task is blocked at two independent points: missing tool (Packer binary/plugin) and, even hypothetically past that, network/credentialed AWS access for the actual build.
tools_used: aws --version (to confirm only aws cli present, no packer)
evidence: Created work dir and wrote a representative ami.pkr.hcl template (Ubuntu 22.04 amazon-ebs source + shell provisioner, per the skill's Basic AMI Template). Ran `which packer` -> command not found. Ran `packer version` -> 'command not found'. Ran `find / -iname "*packer*" -type f 2>/dev/null` -> only unrelated node_modules/pngjs 'packer.js' files, no HashiCorp packer binary. Confirmed aws CLI exists (aws-cli/1.46.1) but that alone cannot run Packer builds or provide the amazon-ebs plugin. Since packer init/validate/build cannot be executed at all, and the network-dependent AWS build step is a further blocker, no AMI template could be validated or built and no deliverable could be produced or verified.
